tags.description: Also known as Shark Point and Batu Tiga (three rocks) off Candidasa. Sloping reef from 5-25m with large gorgonians; nutrient-rich water from the Indonesian Throughflow. Strong and variable/unpredictable currents (not confined to full moon per source consensus). Whitetip reef sharks (often resting in groups of 8+), wobbegong sharks, rare coral catsharks, turtles, giant trevally, occasional blacktip reef sharks and devil rays, mola mola (Jul-Oct, sometimes wider May-Nov window per some operators). Pygmy seahorse claim removed - not confirmed site-specific.
tags.name: Gili Mimpang

tags.description: US Army cargo transport launched 19 June 1918, Federal Shipbuilding Co., Kearny NJ. Sources disagree on length (120-125m) and tonnage (6,211 gross tons per wartime submarine patrol records vs 13,130 tons displacement per Wikipedia). Torpedoed ~04:15 on 11 January 1942 by submarine I-66 (same vessel renumbered I-166 later in 1942 - both names refer to one submarine and are not a contradiction) ~10nm SW of Lombok Strait, carrying rubber and railway parts from Tanjung Priok toward the Philippines. Crew of 54 rescued same day by Dutch flying boat. Towed toward Singaraja by USS Paul Jones and HNLMS Van Ghent but beached at Tulamben around 14 January 1942. Slid into the sea during the 1963 Mount Agung eruption; broke apart at midsection. Sources disagree on distance offshore (10-40m). Confirmed marine life at site: bigeye trevally, sweetlips, hawksbill turtles, Napoleon wrasse, great barracuda, garden eels, bumphead parrotfish (dawn/night), moray eels, occasional reef sharks; macro: frogfish, ghost pipefish, nudibranchs; night: Spanish dancers, flashlight fish.
tags.name: USAT Liberty Wreck

tags.description: North side of Menjangan Island in West Bali National Park. Shallow reef slopes from 5m to 40m+. Rich hard and soft corals, table corals, gorgonian fans, barrel sponges. Clownfish in anemones throughout shallows. Confirmed: bigeye trevally, titan triggerfish, scorpionfish, sea turtles, whitetip/blacktip reef sharks, nudibranchs, pygmy seahorses. Garden eels and grouper claims removed - garden eels are a specialty of the nearby Eel Garden site, not Coral Garden; grouper unconfirmed. Stingrays reported by one source only for deeper sections.
tags.name: Coral Garden

tags.description: East wall of Menjangan Island. Cave entrances at 9-12m depth, wall drops beyond 40m. Bats inhabit caves at waterline giving site its name. Cave crevasses harbour electric clams and moray eels (confirmed). Wall section: large gorgonians, whip corals, barrel sponges. Schools of bluefin/bigeye trevally and fusiliers; blacktip and whitetip reef sharks at depth; octopus in overhangs. One operator source reports occasional whale shark sightings - single-source, not independently corroborated, treat as rare/seasonal only. Nudibranchs/crustaceans/pygmy seahorses removed as unconfirmed site-specific claims. Often dived as a drift continuation from Pos 2, though this pairing is not confirmed as a fixed official plan.
tags.name: Bat Cave

tags.description: Southwest coast of Nusa Penida. Only reef manta rays (Manta alfredi) reported here, no oceanic mantas. Cleaning stations at roughly 5-15m depending on source (one operator cites ~5m, others 10-15m); a separate rock/wall formation (sometimes called Batu Sepatu) extends to 30-40m for advanced divers but is not the shallow cleaning-station experience. Encounter rate varies by source: 90-95% per some operators, more conservatively >50% per others; ScubaBoard notes swell makes the site inaccessible ~10 days/month. Nusa Penida has one of the highest recorded rates of melanistic (all-black) mantas worldwide (~10% of local population), including a regularly-sighted individual nicknamed "Batman", documented at this site. Also: bamboo/nurse sharks, blue-spotted stingrays, turtles, eagle rays, nudibranchs, Zanzibar shrimps, porcelain crabs, mola mola (Jul-Oct, seasonal). Whale sharks reported by multiple operators but consistently described as extremely rare, isolated sightings - not a predictable occurrence. Boat only; fully exposed to Indian Ocean swell.
tags.name: Manta Point

tags.description: Jemeluk Bay, Amed. Balinese temple sculpture on sandy seabed marked by surface buoy. Batfish gather beneath shrine structure - the signature sighting, confirmed by multiple independent sources. Jemeluk Bay reef hosts lionfish, clownfish in anemones, butterflyfish, triggerfish, stingrays, reliable schools of big-mouth mackerel. Garden eels and octopus removed as site-specific claims - those are documented at other nearby Amed sites (Bunutan and Jemeluk Drop Off respectively), not confirmed at the shrine itself. Coral-covered reef around bay perimeter 10-25m.
tags.name: Underwater Shrine

tags.description: Likely the house reef at Bluehill Dive Resort Tulamben, a shallow shore-entry reef (2-15m) between the USAT Liberty Wreck and the Tulamben Wall. Known for statues and stone carvings scattered on the reef. Extensive re-search (ScubaBoard, other Tulamben operators, TripAdvisor, general web) found no independent confirmation of a distinctly named "Blue Hill" dive site beyond the resort's own page - only the resort itself supports the name. Remains single-source and unvalidated; treat with caution pending human review.
tags.name: Blue Hill Dive Site

tags.description: North side of Menjangan Island (corrected from earlier 'western side' - a directly-verified operator source specifically places it on the north side). Sandy-bottomed cavern with entrance reported 10-15m depending on source (one cites ~10m at a 3x4m cavity, another a 6m top with entrance 10-15m). Cave walls: sponges, electric clams (flash in dim light). Juvenile whitetip reef sharks specifically reported sheltering in/near the cave; pygmy seahorses also reported. Grouper, frogfish, anglerfish, and open-water trevally/tuna claims removed - not confirmed by any site-specific source. Wall with gullies and channels. Generally mild currents on this side.
tags.name: Underwater Cave

tags.description: Listed as a dive-site name at Menjangan Island in several directories, generally placed toward the island's western corner. QA pass found a sourcing problem: the previously-cited source (a diveconcepts.com "Crystal Bay Menjangan" page) actually describes Crystal Bay off Nusa Penida/Nusa Lembongan, 100+ km away, with no mention of Menjangan; a diveconcepts.com page literally titled "Blue Corner" also turned out to describe a different Blue Corner at Nusa Lembongan, not Menjangan. Both mismatched sources removed. No genuine site-specific source (depth, current, marine life) for a Menjangan "Blue Corner" could be found - gekodivebali.com and balifundiving.com general Menjangan listings describe the island's other named sites but do not mention this one. Wall/current characterization reflects general type classification only, not a confirmed site-specific description. Not validated pending a genuine source.
tags.name: Blue Corner

tags.description: Menjangan Island main entrance, in front of West Bali National Park ranger station. Gentle sandy slope to 30m. Jetty pilings: ghost pipefish, pipefish, nudibranchs, crustaceans. Sandy slope: garden eels, blue-spotted stingrays, cuttlefish. Batfish near structure. Calm conditions, excellent for training dives.
tags.name: Post I Jetty

tags.description: Western tip of Menjangan Island. Wall drops to ~30m. Good morning light through shallow corals. Dense juvenile fish nurseries in shallow branching corals. Lionfish, ghost pipefish, moray eels on wall. Turtles feeding on reef crest. Reef sharks and trevally at depth. Batfish mid-water. Slightly more sheltered than eastern wall sites.
tags.name: Mangrove Point

tags.description: Northwest Nusa Penida near Broken Beach (Pasih Uug). Sandy bottom slopes from 5m to 12m then to 30m. Reef mantas often seen at 1-6m, no fixed cleaning stations. ~80% encounter rate. Blue-spotted stingrays, reef sharks, turtles on coral bommies. Mola mola possible July-October. Less exposed than Manta Point. Clownfish, moray eels on bommies.
tags.name: Manta Bay

tags.description: Shore-entry wall dive along Amed's northeast Bali coastline. Reef slope drops to wall at ~5m, descends to ~25m. Hard and soft corals, sea fans, sponges. Fusiliers, angelfish, surgeonfish, hawksbill turtles, reef whitetip sharks at depth. Macro: ghost pipefish, frogfish, nudibranchs in sea fans and muck base. Visibility 10-25m. Usually mild currents.
tags.name: Amed wall

tags.description: Sheltered bay east of Padangbai ferry port, east Bali. White sandy bottom with coral bommies starting at 5m, wall section (Tanjung Sari) to 15-18m. Shore entry from beach. Ideal for Open Water certification. Clownfish in anemones abundant. Moray eels, lionfish, sweetlips, turtles, reef sharks on wall, nudibranchs. Night dives: octopus, cuttlefish, lobster. Can have unexpected currents.
tags.name: Blue Lagoon

tags.description: Northern section of Gili Tepekong in Amuk Bay. Less challenging than the south canyon. Huge boulders to swim among and open coral plains. Moderate currents possible but manageable for intermediate divers. Boat dive from Padangbai. Reef and boulder formations 10-25m.
tags.name: Gili Tepekong North

tags.description: The Canyon ('the toilet') - southern section of Gili Tepekong. Dramatic drop-off with swim-through tunnel (28m to 18m), shark boulder, canyon formation. Strong to very strong currents with dangerous downcurrents. Bali's most technically demanding dive site. Whitetip/blacktip reef sharks, sweetlips schools, jacks, groupers, tuna, mola mola (Jul-Oct). Advanced OW + 50 logged dives minimum.
tags.name: Gili Tepekong South

tags.description: Northwest tip of Nusa Penida. Bali's premier site for mola mola (ocean sunfish) July-October; peak August-September. Two shallow reefs on either side of bay plus deep channel to 190m. Powerful downcurrents documented causing multiple accidents and fatalities - advanced divers only. Water temperature drops to 16-18°C during cold upwellings. Mola mola cleaning stations at 20-35m. Also: manta rays, barracuda, giant trevally, whitetip/blacktip reef sharks, turtles, frogfish, wobbegong, nudibranchs.
tags.name: Crystal Bay

tags.description: Also known as Pura Ped, on the sheltered north coast of Nusa Penida near the Pura Ped temple, alongside SD, Sental and Buyuk. Site_type corrected from wall to drift: it is a gently sloping reef (bottom slopes gradually to roughly 15-17m before steepening) rather than a true vertical wall, usually dived as a drift. Current varies from an easy drift most days to occasionally strong. Turtles reliable on the slope; butterflyfish, triggerfish, parrotfish common. Noted by Nusa Penida shops as one of the more reliable north-coast sites for mola mola (Jul-Oct), sometimes ahead of neighboring SD Point. Reef shark and dense pelagic schooling claims removed - not confirmed in current sources.
tags.name: Ped

tags.description: Shore-entry reef in Amed area. Coral clump rising from sandy bottom. Nutrient-rich Lombok Strait waters. Schools of snappers, platax (batfish), fusiliers. Tuna in blue water. Weedy scorpionfish (Rhinopias aphanes) and leaf scorpionfish confirmed. Nudibranchs, crabs, mantis shrimps. 5-30m depth. Nil to moderate current. Good visibility 15-30m.
tags.name: Batu Belah

tags.description: Muck dive in Amed area, boulder entry/exit near a temple. Black volcanic sand with bouldery bottom, rubble, sparse coral. Wunderpus and Cuthona nudibranchs ('sheep nudis') confirmed by ScubaBoard trip reports. 8-25m depth. Mild current. 'Also known as Ghost Bay' claim removed - unconfirmed; Ghost Bay is a separate, distinct Amed site.
tags.name: Bulakan

tags.description: Jemeluk Bay, Amed. Hollow concrete pyramid structures placed by local fishermen in early 1990s as reef enhancement. Now covered in soft corals, sea fans, hard coral. ~18-22m depth. Hawksbill and green turtles at cleaning stations. Blue-spotted stingrays on sandy floor. Frogfish, leaf/stone scorpionfish on pyramids. Pygmy seahorses on pink sea fans. Shore or boat access.
tags.name: Pyramids

tags.description: Shore-entry shallow reef between Liberty Wreck and Drop-off at Tulamben. 3-15m depth. Table corals, staghorn, massive Porites heads on black volcanic sand. Sunken Balinese statues (Buddha, Hindu deities) as focal points. Ghost pipefish, leaf scorpionfish, harlequin shrimp, mantis shrimp, clownfish in large anemone patches, ribbon eels, reef sharks. Night: Spanish dancers. Accessible all levels.
tags.name: Coral Garden Tulamben

tags.description: Southeast point of Menjangan Island. Wall from 12m to 40m+. Most spectacular coral 15-25m: largest sea fans in Bali, whip corals, multi-coloured sponges. Denise pygmy seahorses on gorgonians 20-25m - one of best pygmy seahorse spots in Bali. Dense fusiliers, triggerfish, trevally. Turtles. Cold upwellings; occasional mola mola and manta rays. Connects to Bat Cave for long drift.
tags.name: Menjangan - Pos 2

tags.description: Southeast of Tulamben Bay, ~5 min by jukung. Sloping reef 12-30m+. Hard corals, large barrel sponges, gorgonian sea fans with pygmy seahorses. Garden eels, sweetlips, angelfish, bannerfish, turtles, groupers, cuttlefish, trevally, bumphead parrotfish. Reef sharks at 20-30m. Submerged chair and table as artificial reef on sandy slope. Mild-moderate drift possible.
tags.name: Emerald
Gili Biaha
tags.description: Most remote of Amuk Bay's three Gili islands; ~45 min boat from Padangbai. Black volcanic wall surrounding island drops to 40m+. Shark Cave at ~10-12m depth on northeastern face where whitetip reef sharks rest; schools of glass fish at cave entrance. Strong and unpredictable currents including downcurrents. Confirmed species: whitetip reef sharks, lobsters, crabs, pufferfish, nudibranchs, octopus, cuttlefish, frogfish, leaf scorpionfish, lionfish, turtles, mola mola (seasonal), dolphins. Best Jun-Oct.

tags.name: Drop-off
tags.description: Tulamben Wall - volcanic wall formed by Mount Agung lava flow. Shore entry across pebble beach. Wall top 3-5m drops to 60m+. Shallow aquarium at 5m teems with reef fish. Wall: sponges, gorgonian fans, black coral, crinoids. Whitetip reef sharks, Napoleon wrasse, frogfish, ghost pipefish, nudibranchs. Adjacent to USAT Liberty wreck.

tags.name: Harlequin Slope
tags.description: Black sand muck slope ~200m southeast of USAT Liberty wreck. Named for resident harlequin shrimps found under rocks at depth. Volcanic sand ridges with small coral outcrops. Shore entry. Extensive re-search (dive shops, ScubaBoard, general web) found no second independent source using this site name - most Tulamben operators describe this general muck area informally (e.g. as "Liberty Slope") without the "Harlequin Slope" name. Remains single-source and unvalidated.

tags.name: Seraya Secrets
tags.description: ~3km SE of Tulamben near Seraya village. Three sub-sites: Top Secrets (shallow), Deep Secrets (to ~35m), Noisy Reef (juvenile triggerfish sounds). Silty black volcanic sand - strict buoyancy required. Metal dome artificial structure colonised by soft corals. Confirmed species: nudibranchs (donut, pikachu), harlequin shrimp, Coleman/tiger shrimp, boxer crabs, frogfish, ghost pipefish, pygmy seahorses, blue-spotted stingrays, mimic octopus, moray eels. Night: Spanish dancers. NOTE: No airplane frame exists at this site - earlier description was in error. Third independent source (diveotion.com) confirms depth range and sub-site structure.

tags.name: Liberty Muck
tags.description: Black sand muck area adjacent to USAT Liberty wreck at Tulamben. Shore entry. Sand ridges perpendicular to shore, 12-28m. Real re-search effort (dive shops, ScubaBoard, dive databases) found no third independent source naming this specific site "Liberty Muck" - the muck area beside the wreck is widely described generically by operators but rarely under this exact name. Remains at 2 sources and unvalidated.

tags.name: Kubu Reef
tags.description: Kubu village, 3.5km NW of Tulamben. Sandy ridges with coral outcrops shallowing to deeper reef with small wall beyond 30m. Two sub-sites. Anglerfish (multiple color morphs including yellow, white/clown, black striped), pygmy seahorses on gorgonias, ghost pipefish, barrel sponges. Local porters assist with equipment. Shore entry over rocky shoreline.

tags.name: Kubu Wreck
tags.description: Also known as the Boga Wreck. Dutch-built vessel intentionally sunk September 2012 off Kubu village as an artificial reef. Sources mostly describe her as a former Indonesian government patrol/communications vessel; a minority describe her as a cargo ship. Build year given as 1952 or 1953 depending on source (Netherlands-built); tonnage consistently ~150 tonnes; length reported 35-50m (40m most common). Depth converges around 16-18m (bow) to 37-40m (stern), settling deeper over time per several operators. Distance from shore inconsistently reported (25-300m across sources). VW car, Buddha statues, wooden steering wheel placed on deck as props. Confirmed marine life (2+ sources): moray eels, barracuda, batfish, lionfish, nudibranchs, octopuses, turtles, surgeonfish, fusiliers, angelfish, damselfish, triggerfish.

tags.name: Jemeluk Wall
tags.description: East end of Jemeluk Beach, Amed. Slope steepens to wall dropping 40m or more. Upper slope: small gorgonias, barrel sponges, large pink gorgonia fans, hard corals. Moray eels in crevices, ribbon eels in sandy areas near base of slope, clownfish in anemones on upper slope. Shore entry from beach. ~10 min from Hotel Uyah. Intermediate to Advanced due to depth.

tags.name: Lipah Bay
tags.description: ~12 min from Amed. Sandy slope to 40m with artificial reef structures (coral-colonised), natural coral patches, large bommies with gorgonias and barrel sponges. Confirmed shark nursery site - juvenile whitetip reef sharks regularly found resting under large table corals; McFadyen's dive log describes only a single shark-like animal on one visit, so sightings evidently vary by visit. Turtles regular. Large moray eels. Shore entry over black pebble beach. All levels when calm. Site_type corrected from wall to reef.

tags.name: Barracuda Wall
tags.description: Drift dive from east end of Bunutan Beach heading east-southeast. Also marketed by local operators as "Bunutan Wall" / "The House of Barracudas" - same drift dive, corroborating depth, wall structure, garden eels, and barracuda. Wall densely covered in thousands of barrel sponges and hundreds of gorgonia fans. Large garden eel colonies on sandy bottom - among largest in Amed area. Ribbon eels and moray eels in wall crevices. Very large brain corals. Current-assisted drift; boat follows bubbles for pickup. Third independent source (nofeardiving.com) found, upgrading validation.
